status: WRITTEN, NOT RUN. Running it is an owner go (design ticket 2026-10-30, amendment A1.4). Every number below is fixed before any session of this eval exists; a change after the first session is an amendment with its own timestamp and reason, and a result read before an amendment voids the run.
question: Does Groundworks help or hurt an agent answering real questions about the owner's projects: more correct answers, fewer confidently wrong ones, and at what token cost?
harness: groundworks eval-run (rust/crates/gw-ops/src/eval_run.rs) unchanged: each question in a fresh headless Claude Code session started in an empty folder, plugin off, read tools only; recording off (GROUNDWORKS_NO_RECORD); a third session with no tools grades each answer against the gold answer without knowing the arm. No new harness.

set.source: a FRESH set from `groundworks eval-draw --days 30` over real asks (ask_packet rows, eval runners excluded). The ask-v1 and ask-v2 sets are worn (ask-v2 used as a test set five times by r11) and are not used.
set.size: 47 questions after the owner approves or rewrites each drawn line and sets its category; `groundworks eval-check` must pass on the frozen file (every gold quote found word for word in a tracked file, every trap's premise absent)
set.categories: at least 6 traps (false premise) and at least 6 questions whose gold needs two sources; the rest as drawn
set.freeze: the set file's sha256 is written into this prereg (amendment, before the first session) and checked by the runner's operator before starting
set.never_from: no question drawn from a scan.local_only folder or an isolated project; eval-draw reads ask packets only, which never searched them

pairing: the same 47 questions in both arms, same model, same effort, same budget cap; the unit of analysis is the question (a pair), not the session
grader: opus, no tools, blind to the arm, one retry on bad JSON; verdict correct | partial | wrong | abstained plus a confidently_wrong flag, as eval_run.rs grades them (eval_run.rs:369-377)

metrics.primary_correct: verdict correct per arm, with 95% Wilson intervals
metrics.tokens: tokens per question as Claude Code reports them (input + cache read + cache write + output), median per arm, and per pair which arm used fewer
metrics.tokens_wasted: tokens spent on a question the arm got wrong (verdict wrong, or confidently_wrong), plus tokens the groundworks arm spent above the plain arm on pairs where both answers got the same verdict (help that changed nothing), each summed and reported with its count
metrics.secondary: turns per question; cost in USD as Claude Code reports it; questions where the groundworks arm saw a recorded fact (packet with a fact candidate)

noise_floor: +-4 on 47 correct (the ask-v2 r2-r5 spread on the same set, 44/43/43/42)

decision_rule.helps: groundworks has >= 4 more correct than plain (beyond the noise floor) AND no more confidently_wrong than plain AND tokens not higher by the sign test (fewer tokens on >= 16 of 47 pairs)
decision_rule.costs_less: groundworks uses fewer tokens on >= 32 of 47 pairs (one-sided sign test p = 0.009) AND its correct is within the noise floor of plain (>= plain - 4) AND no more confidently_wrong
decision_rule.hurts: groundworks has >= 4 fewer correct, or more confidently_wrong than plain, or more tokens on >= 32 of 47 pairs with correct within noise
decision_rule.no_evidence: anything else, including overlapping Wilson intervals with a difference inside the noise floor. 'No evidence either way' is a result and is reported as one, never rounded toward help
decision_rule.reported_together: every verdict is printed with the unflattering number next to the flattering one: correct with confidently_wrong, tokens saved with tokens wasted

threats: question answering about the owner's projects is not the whole of the owner's work: coding sessions, builds and releases are not measured here; the meter's before/after trend (groundworks cost) covers them only as a confounded trend
the set is drawn from questions agents asked Groundworks, which may favour the groundworks arm; the plain arm has the same files and read tools, and the traps guard against premise-following
one run per arm: LLM answers vary between runs (+-4 on 47 measured), which is why a difference inside the floor is no evidence
the grader is one model; a sample of 10 pairs is re-graded by the owner blind to the arm and the grader's agreement is reported
budget: 94 answering sessions + 94 grading sessions on the subscription; the ask-v2 r10/r11 runs of 66 cost about $25-33 per arm
outputs: rows appended by eval-run (resumable); the report from eval-report; the verdict line recorded in the groundworks journal as a decision with the run's machine
